Account profile name/bio saves now share a result-bearing updateProfile API. Optional fields become flags in one request; nil means leave unchanged and an empty bio explicitly clears it. Empty responses, userEmpty and mismatched user IDs fail; only an accepted own-user response merges peers and writes the bio cache. Accepted queued transactions survive observer cancellation; cancellation before the response suppresses writes. A successful earlier save leaves subsequent edits open. Explicit bio edit state preserves drafts before delayed cache arrival, allows missing-cache edits, hydrates untouched bios after name edits, survives copy methods and participates in equality. Missing input data no longer clears the draft. Thirty-four tests execute the full save helper, actual validation/update/lifecycle closures, valuesRequiringUpdate, and EditInfoState except its context-dependent initializer. Real SwiftSignalKit with modeled UI/network/progress boundaries: 30 controller/state comparison cases, 22 fail on original source with 40 assertions, plus 4 helper-only lifecycle/reentry cases. Full factory rendering, avatars, notes, birthday/business state, real progress/navigation and live server behavior remain partial.

Only accepted requests update current CachedUserData, creating it when absent and preserving other fields/peers. Cold and pending signals capture Postbox/peerId instead of Account; cancellation before a response suppresses work, while an already accepted queued commit survives observer cancellation. Twenty-four tests extract all birthday value/API mapping and mutation code with real SwiftSignalKit and modeled transport/Postbox. All pass; the saved original fails 7 cases with 15 assertions. Native Birthdays primary-file checking passes. Profile birthday add/remove now share an owned, coalesced save action. Twenty-four tests extract the actual calendar selection callback, removal closure, local birthday request closure, public helper and lifecycle hooks, plus the complete save action. Real SwiftSignalKit with modeled controller/progress/network boundaries. All 24 pass; original callbacks fail 17 cases with 21 assertions. Existing 34 profile-editor tests still pass. Native full editor and save-action primary-file checks pass. Actual calendar/modal appearance, same-window account switches, global originating-screen lifetimes and international/date-without-year conversion remain unverified.

Calendar and birthday date integrity: hidden-year selection uses leap year 4, with legacy year 1 still decoded as absent. Calendar labels/menu/navigation use the shared hidden-year convention. Hiding a year and opening a suggested birthday preserve February 29. Gregorian date conversion, birthday eligibility/age, suggested-date construction and formatting are independent of the system calendar; invalid day/month/year combinations are rejected rather than silently normalized. Gregorian display retains localized month/date formatting. Calendar month alignment derives the first calendar day rather than subtracting fixed 86400-second days, preventing DST column shifts. Day eligibility compares whole local calendar dates, enforces inclusive future/one-year/explicit limits across month/year boundaries and rejects invalid day indices; navigation cannot continue farther outside the allowed range. Fifty tests compile actual Objective-C CalendarUtils and extract the full month model, native navigation/label/hide-year handlers, Date birthday conversion, birthday helpers/formatter and chat suggested-date construction. Real Foundation calendars/DateFormatter across multiple time zones, DST and Buddhist/Islamic/Japanese calendars; Calendar.current/Locale.current/Date() are injected only at test seams for reproducibility, and UI widgets are modeled. All 50 pass; original sources fail 35 cases with 64 assertions. Six native Swift primary-file checks pass; ChatServiceItem uses a signature shim for dateForPicker, separately typechecked in TelegramUtils. Localization layout, calendar accessibility, global preference changes mid-picker, extreme dates, actual date-preview fetching and suggested-birthday modal lifecycle remain partial.

Calendar confirmation now stores the selected date independently of the browsed month. Actual day clicks update it before callbacks/closing; browsing months does not replace it, and returning to the selected month restores the correct highlight. Year changes preserve/clamp the selected day within the month and enforce picker year/future/explicit limits; hiding a year uses the selected date and is unavailable for future-only/disabled pickers. The date accessor no longer force-casts the current navigation child. Picker disappearance/deinit invalidates retained selection/navigation callbacks, reappearance allows fresh selection, and autoclose becomes inactive before dismissal to prevent reentrant/duplicate callbacks. Chat suggested-birthday Save reads the selected date, submits once, rejects accept/hide-year callbacks after disappearance and no longer captures AccountContext through retained accept callbacks. Thirty-eight tests compile the full CalendarController, exact CalendarMonthController initializer/navigation getters, full CalendarMonthStruct, actual day click closure and chat modal accept/hide/lifecycle fragments, with real Objective-C CalendarUtils/Foundation and modeled UI/navigation. All 38 pass. Of 37 safe original-source cases, 33 fail with 48 assertions; the separately isolated original date-getter case aborts with signal 6 on a forced cast, giving 34 failing original cases overall. Existing 50 calendar-date cases still pass after fixture updates. Both native CalendarController and full ChatServiceItem primary-file checks pass; chat uses the previously separately typechecked dateForPicker signature shim. Main app not built. Actual popover/modal animation lifecycle, visual selection/keyboard behavior and originating-account changes remain unverified. Chat still closes after initiating its existing standalone birthday hook; acknowledgement/error lifecycle beyond selection is not claimed fixed.

Pending clicks coalesce; acceptance closes only if the selected birthday still matches the submitted snapshot. A changed selection stays open. Twenty-six exact-source tests execute the full ChatBirthdaySaveAction plus modal accept/hide/lifecycle closures with real SwiftSignalKit and modeled UI/progress/network endpoints. Full ChatServiceItem and ChatBirthdaySaveAction native primary-file checks both report exit 0 against cached dependencies; the chat check retains the previously separately verified dateForPicker signature shim. Actual AppKit progress/modal lifecycle, same-window account switching and live server cancellation/commit ordering remain unverified. No main app build.

Profile photo/video updates now share one owned operation from image preparation or video generation through editor results and upload. Cancellation, screen removal/deinit and newer selections dispose pending work immediately. A generation predicate rejects stale/reentrant callbacks; cancellation cannot clear a newer operation started during disposal. Only one image, prepared path and editor result are consumed. Video handling reaches UI work on the main queue, accepts one terminal generator result, ignores late progress/duplicate completion, initializes upload progress even without a start event and clears progress when generation ends without a result. The progress cancel callback captures the operation, state Promise and state Atomic weakly, preventing the progress state from retaining itself through its stored callback; retained cancel callbacks no longer keep that state alive after screen deinit. Thirty-six tests extract the exact photo/video/cancel and screen-removal/deinit closures plus the whole operation helper, using real SwiftSignalKit and modeled image preparation, editor, engine and UI state. All 36 pass; original code fails 25 cases with 40 assertions. Full EditAccountInfoController and EditAccountPhotoAction native primary-file checks report exit 0 against cached dependencies; the profile check retains the separately verified updateProfile API signature shim. Actual media generation, temporary files, UI presentation and queue scheduling are modeled; no main app build.

MediaObjectToAvatar no longer self-retains until a successful result. start() now returns a cold signal; each subscription creates and retains its own generator until completion/disposal, without retaining the originating generator object. Cancelled/failed/empty operations and unused signals no longer depend on a later successful value to break a self-cycle. Ten exact-wrapper tests use real SwiftSignalKit with controlled generation and weak lifetime probes; all pass. The original wrapper is tested with expensive rendering/fetch setup replaced by the same controlled endpoint, retaining its actual holder/afterNext ownership logic; it fails eight cases with ten assertions, including unsubscribed work, cancellation, empty/failure lifetime and shared-operation behavior. The normal successful baseline cleanup is allowed its original main-queue delay. Full MediaObjectToAvatar native primary-file checking passes. Underlying AVAssetWriter/decoder/fetch cancellation, queued conversion work and temporary-file cleanup are not proven by this wrapper harness. Generator terminal-result follow-up: MediaObjectToAvatar.start now forwards progress until one successful result or explicit failure, then completes/disposes once. A source that completes without a result emits an explicit failure. Animated source failures retain the failed status, and static adapters do not translate terminal failure into never(). Four additional wrapper tests bring the suite to 14 passing cases. The immediate pre-change wrapper fails the four new cases with 9 assertions. The original pre-ownership wrapper fails 12 of all 14 cases with 19 assertions; the normal successful original cleanup retains its main-queue timing allowance. Rendering remains controlled in this lifetime suite.

Avatar video export replaces the AVAssetWriterInput busy-wait loop with serial readiness callbacks. Writer configuration/start/append/final completion are validated, rejected/failed/cancelled writes cannot publish a path, status observation catches failure while backpressured, reentrant cancellation is checked before append, completion is single-use, and failed/cancelled partial output is removed. Export callbacks capture the exporter weakly. A frame sequence validates bounds/rates, uses exclusive end frames, begins timestamps at zero, preserves source duration and caps output at 30 fps without the former fixed-30 timing/skipping errors; Lottie uses its native source rate. Twenty-eight isolated tests pass: 16 controlled full-writer cases, 8 frame-sequence cases, and 4 native AVFoundation cases. Native H.264 produced a readable 640x640 video with the expected one-second duration; actual render failure and cancellation also exercised the real writer. No original-source executable comparison was made for the new writer API; baseline failing-test count is zero/unknown, not a claim of no original defects. Full native primary-file checking passes against cached dependencies. Apple documentation and telegram-ios MediaEditorVideoAVAssetWriter corroborate readiness-driven supply. Live codec/device diversity and every supported sticker format remain unverified.

StickerToMp4Context now consumes preparation once, reports exporter/renderer/metadata/first-frame/thumbnail/pixel-buffer/render/finalization failure, and cancels fetch/export work with a shared atomic cancellation flag that is visible while the conversion queue is busy. Wrapper cancellation/deinit invalidates the flag before queue cleanup. Output completion is fenced; failed thumbnails and rejected output paths are deleted, while successful outputs transfer to the consumer and survive context release. The first rendered frame is reused, later frames receive the prior frame for decoder/cache dependencies, and a short WebM finishes at its detected endpoint instead of treating decoder end as a render error. Twenty-three tests compile the complete production StickerToMp4Context and actual frame sequence with real SwiftSignalKit, CoreMedia and filesystem operations; rendering, resource fetching and writer completion are controlled fixtures. All pass. Full MediaObjectToAvatar native primary-file checking passes. No executable original-context comparison was made because its nested writer/monolithic synchronous loop has a different interface; baseline failing count is zero/unknown. Real Lottie/WebM/WebP decoder behavior, failed download signaling, empty-background signals, extremely long exports, image allocation failures and live UI remain unverified. Typed source-error follow-up: StickerToMp4Context now consumes avatarMediaResourcePath, so failed downloads terminate conversion; an empty background also produces failure when preparation completes without a tuple. The completed callback distinguishes preparation that has actually started rendering so it cannot reject an ongoing export. Three additional full-context cases bring that suite to 26 passing cases; fetch endpoint behavior is modeled there and separately exercised with real SwiftSignalKit in avatar-media-preparation. Native full-source checking passes. Rendering follow-up: thumbnail compositing failure now has a terminal-failure regression; 27 cases pass. Empty-background follow-up: combineLatest waits for both sources to complete, so a completed background without an image previously kept a pending sticker download alive. Both static and animated paths now turn empty background completion into a typed failure before taking the first image. Two synchronous/asynchronous pending-download cases per path fail on the immediately preceding snapshot (4 cases, 8 assertions) and pass after the fix. All 29 conversion cases and all 39 media-preparation cases pass. Full native MediaObjectToAvatar primary-file checking passes. This covers an explicitly completed empty background, not a wallpaper source that never emits or completes.

Avatar source preparation now uses a typed fetchedMediaResource path instead of swallowing fetch errors. Fetch completion without next is valid; resource data is read after accepted completion, incomplete data is ignored, one complete path is consumed, and empty data completion becomes failure. The helper retains MediaBox rather than AccountContext. Static sticker decoding/read failures and empty backgrounds produce a terminal result; repeated starts/data/background updates do not repeat work. GIF/video sources validate a copied video, extract a transformed JPEG thumbnail and only then publish both paths; copy/decode/thumbnail failure never publishes a fake path. Prepared files are owned until takeFiles transfers them and are removed if unclaimed. makeAvatarVideo now routes static stickers through photo handling, and static failure/unexpected results complete instead of returning a never-ending inner signal. The profile controller uses this shared adapter. Thirty-six tests pass: 22 exact-source typed-fetch/source lifecycle cases, 8 full-adapter cases and 6 native AVFoundation/ImageIO/filesystem cases. Native cases verify real copied MP4 bytes/duration, JPEG readability/dimensions, missing/invalid/directory sources, unclaimed cleanup and transferred-file survival. The original adapter fails 4 of its 8 cases with 7 assertions; the other 28 preparation tests have no original-source executable comparison. Native checks pass for MediaObjectToAvatar, AvatarMediaPreparation, MakeAvatarVideo and the profile caller. Live network/database ordering, real WebP decoding, native UI error feedback and file cleanup after paths have already transferred remain unverified. Rendering follow-up: static sticker compositing failure now has a terminal-failure regression; 37 cases pass. Empty-background follow-up: combineLatest waits for both sources to complete, so a completed background without an image previously kept a pending sticker download alive. Both static and animated paths now turn empty background completion into a typed failure before taking the first image. Two synchronous/asynchronous pending-download cases per path fail on the immediately preceding snapshot (4 cases, 8 assertions) and pass after the fix. All 29 conversion cases and all 39 media-preparation cases pass. Full native MediaObjectToAvatar primary-file checking passes. This covers an explicitly completed empty background, not a wallpaper source that never emits or completes. Its cumulative baseline count includes 4 shared-adapter failures from the earlier comparison and 2 empty-background failures from the later snapshot.

Avatar bitmap generation now uses a local failable Core Graphics context. Canvas dimensions and drawing transforms reject non-finite, non-positive and overflowing values before allocation; output dimensions use source pixels rather than display backing scale. Pixel-buffer creation, locking, base address and context creation are checked, with exactly one unlock after a successful lock. Thumbnail/static compositing failures terminate their generators. Color gradients and emoji bitmap creation no longer force-unwrap failed output. Pattern backgrounds wait for completed decodable data, accept one final image, dispose the source and reject missing data/context/image instead of accepting a loading placeholder. Thirty-five rendering tests pass: 12 native Core Graphics/Core Video pixel/geometry cases, 12 controlled allocation/locking/extraction cases, and 11 exact-helper pattern cases using real SwiftSignalKit/ImageIO with a modeled transform. Nine safe pattern cases were compared with the pre-rendering snapshot: six fail with 11 assertions; two original forced-unwrap cases were skipped, not counted as reproduced crashes. The conversion and media-preparation suites also pass with 27 and 37 cases after adding one compositing-failure case each. Native primary-file checks pass for MediaObjectToAvatar and AvatarImageRendering. Full app rendering, display/codec diversity, actual memory pressure and shared DrawingContext internals remain unverified; the shared pattern renderer still has its own unchecked allocation path.

Profile avatar file-panel and constructor callbacks now use a screen-owned single-use acquisition. A newer selection invalidates the previous callback; cancellation/nil selection consumes it; disappearance, removal and deinit release pending selected closures. Callbacks retain the owner weakly instead of retaining context/update closures after cancellation. Presentation requires the original loaded controller and window and the same context window; an appearance identity prevents old menu actions from reviving after navigation away and back. Reentrant selection/presentation checks cannot replace a newer request. Thirty-five exact-source isolated tests pass: 25 menu-factory/lifecycle cases with modeled AppKit/file-panel/constructor boundaries and 10 complete-owner cases. The previous menu factory fails 21 of its 25 comparison cases with 25 assertions; helper-only cases use current code and are not original comparisons. Existing profile-editor 34, birthday-ui 24 and profile-photo 36 tests pass (129 focused cases total). Full native primary-file checks pass for EditAccountInfoController and EditAccountAvatarAcquisition against cached dependencies; the profile checker still uses the previously verified updateProfile signature shim. No main app build, live native sheet/modal interaction, real same-window account switch or Instruments measurement was performed.

VideoAvatarModalController now delegates trimmed video export to an owned asynchronous exporter. Trim bounds/durations/non-finite values are validated; thumbnail time is clamped inside the selected range and the uploaded key-frame timestamp is relative to the trim start, then bounded by actual output duration. The 0.05-second endpoint margin and relative timestamp agree with telegram-ios PeerInfoScreenAvatarSetup. Session creation and MP4 support, thumbnail decoding/destination/finalization, final export status/error and readable output duration/video tracks are checked. Failed/cancelled/unclaimed partial files are removed, including files recreated by late completion after cancellation; successful paths transfer to the existing consumer contract. Timers stop on termination and hold the operation weakly; progress is finite and clamped. Startup uses Queue.justDispatch because Queue.async executes inline on its own queue and could start work before a cancellation handle was installed. Thirty-three isolated tests pass: 21 full-exporter controlled AVFoundation/ImageIO cases using real SwiftSignalKit/timers/filesystem, 8 native CMTime range cases and 4 real AVFoundation cases. A generated H.264 source produced a readable 0.6-second trimmed MP4 with a 0.3-second relative cover timestamp and a readable 640x640 JPEG; invalid preset, empty composition and cancellation after thumbnail creation were also checked natively. Six safe timing cases run against exact earlier timing expressions from commit 6bb9f7ec39259d7a4537820620f775bd82b8becf; five fail with nine assertions. This comparison does not execute the full old export lifecycle or reproduce its forced-unwrap crashes. Native primary-file checks pass for EditedAvatarVideoExport and the complete VideoAvatarModalController; the harness fully compiles the exporter. No app build or live editor UI validation.

Video avatar preparation now returns the copied composition track, preserving its preferred transform, and both preview/export instructions reference that track rather than the source asset track. Missing/invalid input returns an explicit terminal error instead of leaving the caller without a signal. Geometry uses the transformed source rectangle and normalizes its origin, preserving reflections and arbitrary affine transforms instead of guessing one of four rotations. Crop mapping validates finite nonzero video/view/selection geometry, bounds the crop, keeps positive encoder dimensions for tiny selections and scales the selected region to the rounded output dimensions. The controller rejects unavailable crop composition before export and thumbnail generation; invalid Enter remains consumed by the modal. Thumbnail count conversion is checked. Twenty-six tests pass: 14 native Core Graphics geometry cases, 5 native preparation/export cases, 3 real mirrored/rotated pixel comparisons and 4 exact selectVideoAvatar routing cases with modeled modal/window endpoints. A source composition using track ID 42 is copied into a new track and renders successfully with instructions targeting the new ID. A mirrored 320x320 crop exports a readable MP4 whose pixels match its preview. Seven native crop/routing cases run against the exact earlier methods from commit 6bb9f7ec39259d7a4537820620f775bd82b8becf; five fail with nine assertions. Native full-controller and helper primary-file checks pass. The crop comparison retains the current preparation fixture and substitutes only the old crop method; routing compares the actual old selection function. No full UI/AppKit presentation, every crop interaction, real-world portrait/VFR/codec matrix or Instruments coverage is claimed.

Avatar playback now seeks to the actual trim start rather than adding an offset proportional to the entire source duration, sets forwardPlaybackEndTime, and clamps suspended seeks inside the selected interval. Each playback generation owns its periodic/end callbacks; obsolete or hidden-editor callbacks cannot move the playhead or restart playback. Reappearance preserves pause state. Initial min/max trim distances are normalized for short clips and do not depend on laid-out width; invalid/sub-millisecond durations reject initialization. Moving a trim interval preserves its duration at both boundaries. Thirty-three exact-source isolated tests pass with real CoreMedia/SwiftSignalKit and modeled player, notification and control endpoints. The original safe comparison contains 32 applicable cases (the new sub-millisecond helper case is excluded); 23 fail with 35 assertions. Native helper, scrubber and full-controller primary-file checks pass. Native AVPlayer seek/event scheduling, live editor gestures and Instruments remain unverified.

Video avatar scrubber handles now sit outside a shared inset timeline, so a ten-second selection on a ten-minute source retains a positive range hit area instead of overlapping handles and negative geometry. Layout, all drag paths, clicks/long presses, darkened trim masks, thumbnails and cover preview/dot positions share that coordinate mapping. Playhead centers clamp to the selected range; zero/tiny bounds cannot create negative sizes. Detached controls, zero-width tracks and non-finite pointer coordinates do not mutate selection. Frame drags clamp at trim endpoints and can move back immediately. Thirty-two exact-source isolated tests pass: 28 layout/gesture cases using modeled view/window endpoints, two native Core Graphics mask-pixel cases, and two actual controller preview-position expressions. All 32 run against the pre-geometry snapshot; 30 fail with 77 assertions. The adjacent 33 playback cases still pass, and native full scrubber/controller primary-file checks pass. No full app build or live AppKit hit-testing/animation validation. Extremely narrow but positive hit regions still need a usability/zoom review; cover-preview lifecycle now has a separate 46-case suite. Four additional gesture cases verify that range/handle drags and clicks clear a pending preview suspension, so release can resume playback without relying on an obsolete animation completion.

Avatar cover previews now own one generation from image request through flash/move animation and click handling. New selection, clearing, crop replacement and disappearance invalidate obsolete callbacks, dispose subscriptions and remove pending views immediately; cancelled animations cannot restore detached previews or retained view references. Requested frames are marked before asynchronous delivery to coalesce repeated player updates, take one result, and install a nested disposable before starting work. Nil/empty images and unavailable composition release preview suspension. Cover requests use the validated trimmed thumbnail time. Crop timelines no longer carry an old cover image through combineLatest; crop requests are coalesced at scheduling, replaced by generation and cancelled on hide, then restarted on reappearance. Non-animated cover replacement completes synchronously. Interaction identity prevents old completions from resuming newer user actions; explicit pending-preview resume intent preserves manual pauses during crop refresh. Actual playback/seek methods verify that completing a cover preview resumes from the cover, and clicking a cover while paused seeks there without jumping to the trim start. Obsolete value emissions cannot update playback. Forty-six isolated tests pass using exact controller/view/animation methods, real SwiftSignalKit/CoreMedia, modeled image generators/player/views/CAAnimation callbacks, and two real background-to-main-queue delivery cases. The saved pre-preview-lifetime source runs all 46 cases; 32 fail with 50 assertions. The expanded 32-case scrubber suite and adjacent 33-case playback suite pass, for 111 focused cases. Full-controller and scrubber primary-file typechecks pass. Image-generation delay is modeled as immediate in this harness; real AVFoundation decoding/cancellation, CAAnimation scheduling, resize rendering and live AppKit/Instruments remain pending.

Shared video thumbnail generation now runs in an owned request with a serial callback queue, atomic cancellation and a retained AVAssetImageGenerator. Requested timestamps determine output slots; duplicate and unexpected callbacks cannot consume slots or replace accepted images. Failed, cancelled and nil-image results count toward completion, including all-failed/empty assets. Missing slots use a blurred or nearest available fallback while successful slots retain their timeline positions. Samples are generated with CoreMedia ratios, coalescing duplicate representable times and staying before duration even near the timescale limit. Invalid/non-finite duration, dimensions, counts and preview times terminate safely; requests are bounded to 4096 samples and 4096 pixels per scaled dimension. Cancellation calls cancelAllCGImageGeneration and clears callback/image ownership even when the backend never replies. Preview decoding is asynchronous/cancellable; the separate small image now honors lowSize and aspect ratio. Bitmap allocation is failable, and placeholder blur uses checked Accelerate vImage processing rather than unchecked DrawingContext/FastBlur allocations. Thirty-seven full-source tests pass: 31 controlled callback/configuration/ownership/validation cases using real SwiftSignalKit/CoreMedia/CoreGraphics/Accelerate, and six real AVFoundation cases using generated H.264 media. Native checks cover normal strips, small preview dimensions, explicit video composition geometry, empty/gapped sources and out-of-duration preview rejection. Native full-file primary typecheck passes. The original source at 489ec8d18bbba43bf9bed52f31c28a35c3e6fde2 matches the saved snapshot byte-for-byte; 31 safe comparisons run, 21 fail with 33 assertions, and six original unsafe-input/concurrent-array-mutation cases are skipped. Output scale is modeled as 2 in the harness; live display-scale changes, AppKit presentation, decoder/codec diversity, actual memory pressure and cancellation latency under load remain pending. Public signatures are unchanged for avatar, ImageCanvas video editing and chat recording trim consumers.

Recording trim thumbnails now invalidate and cancel immediately on every setVideo call, including same-path content replacement, and clear previous media before a new placeholder/decode. Cache identity includes scaled thumbnail dimensions as well as path/count. A nested request disposable and generation guard protect synchronous replacement and queued main-thread results; detaching from a window or switching to audio cancels pending work, and reattachment schedules a fresh request. Thumbnail strips distribute all samples across the available width instead of using source aspect widths that leave gaps or hide later frames. Recording and ImageCanvas callers validate finite positive dimensions, scaled decode sizes and exact bounded Int sample counts before conversion/allocation. ImageCanvas thumbnail requests also include scaled size, cancel on disappearance and restart on appearance; closed/hidden views reject results and new work. Its play/end/seek/periodic callbacks now respect presentation/closing state, seek-resume intent is cleared on disappearance, and paused controls are updated before returning. Forty exact-source isolated cases pass: 18 recording request/lifecycle cases, 18 editor request/playback/lifecycle cases and four strip-layout cases, with real SwiftSignalKit and controlled thumbnail/view/player endpoints. Both full native source primary-file typechecks pass; ImageCanvas typechecking includes the existing Xcode-generated asset-symbol source rather than asset API stubs. Thirty-eight safe comparisons against saved pre-change files run; 28 fail with 33 assertions. Two unchecked old non-finite count-conversion tests are skipped to avoid trapping the test process. No full app build, live window/display movement, actual recording pause/resume device integration or CA/AppKit rendering validation is claimed.

Recording preview application and trim callbacks normalize finite positive durations and intersect retained selections safely; empty or disjoint selections reset to the full new preview instead of constructing an inverted range. Invalid preview durations and trim callbacks without a preview are ignored. RecordingTrimScrubberView normalizes range/position, invalidates drags on source/range/mode replacement, detach and resize, rejects detached/non-finite gestures and keeps progress-only and own-trim updates active. Handles, seek mapping, waveform selection and playhead share one inset source timeline; pixel-rounded endpoints remain reachable and zero/tiny frames have bounded selection geometry. Stationary drags do not unexpectedly expand existing narrow trims. Waveform sample counts and duration labels use checked numeric conversion. Forty-six exact-source harness cases pass with native Cocoa/CoreGraphics geometry/drawing and modeled recorder/player/view endpoints. The adjacent 40 thumbnail caller tests remain green. Both full recording scrubber and recording input native primary-file typechecks pass against cached dependencies. No full app build or live recording/window integration is claimed.

Recording resume now returns an acknowledged Bool result from a cold signal: selection stays intact while trimming, false/empty completion does not resume, only the first result is used, cancelled/changed-source requests cannot restart recording, and a successful result already queued from the backend still clears the applied selection if UI cancellation prevents automatic resume. ChatInputRecordingView keeps preview metadata while pending, disables duplicate resume/trim/send actions, restores preview controls and shows an error on rejection, supports retry, uses nested disposable ownership for synchronous callbacks, and cancels pending work on reset/discard/detach. VideoRecorderPipeline guards queued composition/export/commit steps against cancellation, discard and resumed recording; abandoned queued outputs are removed and accepted trims publish their new paused preview path/duration. Forty-six exact-source cases pass with real SwiftSignalKit and controlled recorder/UI/export endpoints, including background result delivery and weak-owner release. The expanded baseline runs 45 cases; 37 fail with 60 assertions. The newly representable composition-failure result case is excluded from the old API comparison. The adjacent 46 recording-trim cases still pass. Both recorder primary-file checks pass; the full real MediaRecorderUI module emits successfully into a temporary directory, and recording input typechecks against that updated interface. No full app build, live device recording, native export cancellation or audio filesystem rollback validation is claimed. Two added cases verify explicit composition failure returns false without starting trim/export and that a pending composition callback does not retain its released pipeline. The original optional-result adapter is used only to align signatures; the new nil-composition case is excluded from baseline counts.

Audio trim/store and native Opus continuity: replacement validates the candidate encoder against memory before atomically replacing disk contents, preserving the paused original on failure. Trim input/output bounds, exact sample conversion, decoder/frame/finalization errors, output collisions and persisted bytes are checked; abandoned partial files are removed. Paused trimming finalizes a cloned snapshot to retain pending PCM and encoder delay. The native encoder buffers partial PCM, submits correct final EOS granules including pre-skip, flushes live pages, and preserves encoder/Ogg state across same-instance and JSON/new-instance pause/resume. Snapshots validate version, architecture, sizes, numeric fields and data/state digests. Review retained hidden-year link behavior if navigation replaces the calendar child, invalid/extreme initial dates, same-window account switching and server response/commit ordering. The asynchronous writer/timing suite has 28 cases including four real AVFoundation cases; full conversion context has 29 cases; typed fetch/source preparation/shared routing has 39 cases including six real video/JPEG/filesystem checks. Typed fetch errors, static decode failures and empty animated backgrounds now terminate. GIF/video sources validate copies and produce thumbnails; unclaimed prepared files clean themselves up. Still validate live Lottie/WebM/WebP samples, renderer/cache behavior, variable-duration WebP, WebM initial 180-frame bound, very long clips, color/orientation, unavailable encoders, native UI error feedback and cancellation under load. Local bitmap/pixel-buffer failure handling and completed-pattern readiness now have 35 rendering cases. Other photo/video callers and same-window account switching remain partial.

Playback/initial trim/range-drag handling now has 33 tests; shared scrubber geometry and gestures have 32 tests. Preview generation/animation/lifecycle has 46 focused cases. Modal UI remains partial. Still audit real-world portrait/multi-track/VFR inputs, empty/gapped track time ranges, source videos whose audio outlasts video, native short-clip playback, real mid-encode cancellation, codec/preset/device diversity and user-visible unsupported/corrupt file feedback. returnKeyAction still creates a Promise per invocation and its optional confirmation maps non-thumbnail states to never(); inspect repeated submit, confirmation rejection, close-before-submit/completion and retained completeState ownership. Raw output paths transfer before downstream delivery; cancellation between successful export and delayed consumer acceptance, including cached Promise results, requires an end-to-end owned-result audit. The new exporter removes files it still owns, not paths already handed to consumers. Preview/crop mouse and resize interaction, pending thumbnail replacement, native account/window lifecycle (including the constructor contentView force unwrap), caller feedback and live screen/Instruments validation remain pending. Key-frame preview request/view generations, hidden/replaced editor callbacks, user interactions, crop replacement, pause intent and background main-queue delivery now have isolated coverage. Real animation timing and end-to-end controller rendering still need native validation. Native AVPlayer asynchronous seek/loop scheduling and extreme-source-length timeline usability remain pending. Shared thumbnail generation now has 37 cases covering failure completion, timestamp ordering, cancellation/ownership, small-image resizing, invalid input and native composition decoding. Still inspect live decoder cancellation latency, remote/damaged assets, device/display scale, sustained resource pressure and user-visible missing-frame feedback. RecordingTrimScrubberView and EditVideoController now have finite sizing/count guards, request-generation ownership, replacement/disappearance cancellation and 40 caller cases. Full native controller checks pass; live recording/editor integration remains partial.

Recording trim and ImageCanvas video editor follow-up: thumbnail identities, sizing, replacement/detach cancellation, tiled frame coverage and hidden playback callbacks have 40 cases. Recording range normalization, safe shorter-preview intersection, waveform numeric conversion, gesture invalidation, source-coordinate alignment and small-frame geometry now have 46 passing cases, including five separately confirmed original crashes. Still audit RecordingPreviewPlayer stale status/end callbacks, seek generation and non-finite timestamps; ChatInputRecordingView live pause/resume/confirmation lifecycle; and ChatRecordingState trim/export result handling. Recording send preparation and direct audio/video fallback rejection now have 41 cases; continue auditing finalization acknowledgement and output ownership. The core recorder updateTrimRange still accepts unvalidated ranges. applyTrimAndResume acknowledgement, selection retention, cold execution, cancellation and UI failure/retry/lifecycle now have 44 cases. Video trim cancellation/discard checks and updated paused preview metadata are covered in those tests. Backend commit vs disposal before the producer publishes its result remains an integration race to audit; already-delivered background success now records applied trim without resuming if UI cancelled before main delivery. Native gesture hit testing, source-scale thumbnail appearance and paused preview feedback remain unverified. ImageCanvas still needs comprehensive constructor trim validation (including persisted non-finite start/end), short-clip seek/end policy, asynchronous crop/paint/tools completions after closing/account changes, repeated discard confirmations, export result ownership and delayed playback callbacks across hide/reappear/new seeks. Validate native display changes and window relocation trigger required layout, real recorder pause/resume and same-path rewritten files; same-path setVideo deliberately reloads because recorder preview contents may have changed.

Transactional audio replacement and native continuity have 64 cases. Video passthroughExport cancellation/completion ownership can leave a completed but undelivered output; Composition now rejects missing/invalid segments, insertion errors and failed/empty exports; 31 composition cases pass and paused payload notifications have 22 cases. However pause/finalization composition failure still uses terminal .failed UI handling and closes the recording; implement retry with retained original segments and feedback. Validate selected trim ranges against actual assets. VideoRecorderPipeline.applyTrim still needs exactly-once completion and transactional concurrent-request handling. Failure after accepted trim during finalization or media extraction can still clear UI; audit full send preparation through actual media acknowledgement. A backend commit before cancellation but before publishing acknowledgement remains a race. Direct video data export transfers raw paths before main-thread delivery and can orphan output on cancellation. New trimmed paused preview uses the existing thumbnail; refresh first-frame thumbnail/modal preview timebase. RecordingPreviewPlayer status/seek/end ordering and invalid timestamps remain unaudited.

Native Opus follow-up: the former finalization, append, malformed-input cleanup and pause/resume defects now have 64 passing trim/store/native cases. Still audit actual AudioUnit callback ordering after pause/teardown, allocation failures, codec/platform diversity, long-recording append decode/reencode CPU/memory/quality, native snapshot portability, disk-full writes and live-upload behavior. DataItem.appendData can still advance memory despite disk-write failure. Paused preview files are still unfinalized even though trim input now finalizes a clone; inspect pending encoder-delay/partial-PCM availability in takePreviewData. RFC 7845 and libopus contiguous-state documentation informed the codec fixes; real hardware and Instruments remain unverified.

Check didFail callback queue/identity, stop/pause pending recorder completion and duration-limit automatic submission (which bypasses ChatRecordingState.send). Add native/device lifecycle evidence before marking recording complete.

last_pass.limitations: Recording pipeline state equality now compares associated preview/path/duration/waveform/upload identity and thumbnail identity instead of treating all paused, finished, stopped or thumbnail states as equal. This allows ValuePromise(ignoreRepeated: true) to publish a newly trimmed paused preview while preserving suppression of genuinely unchanged snapshots. Twenty-two exact-source isolated tests pass using the actual ChatRecordingPreviewData and VideoCameraRecordingStatus definitions, real SwiftSignalKit ValuePromise and native Core Graphics images; the waveform value type alone is modeled. Fifteen of the 22 original-code cases fail with 16 assertions. Covers individual payload changes, same-value suppression, all case pairs and an integrated pause/trim/resume notification sequence. Full native MediaRecorderUI module emission passes. Live modal playback/rendering after a new state remains unverified. Recording segment composition now fails explicitly if any segment is missing/unreadable, its video timing is invalid or insertion throws, rather than silently dropping that segment. An export failure or empty completion no longer substitutes the last segment with aggregate metadata. Single and joined output durations come from readable actual assets and are checked before Int conversion. Existing composed preview storage remains intact until replacement succeeds; stale/changed-source/discarded results are rejected and their queued output paths removed. Request identity invalidates older queued joins; one export result is accepted. Preview/finalization/trim callbacks avoid strong owner cycles, and obsolete finalization cannot overwrite resumed recording or publish discarded media. Thirty-one tests pass: 25 exact pipeline-method cases with modeled AVFoundation/export/filesystem endpoints and six native AVFoundation cases. Native tests generate H.264 media, reject missing/corrupt sources, verify actual duration, join one- and two-second sources into a readable three-second MP4 and decode frames from both segments. The 25 original-method comparisons fail 22 cases with 36 assertions; the baseline adapter only wraps its two-argument completion into the new optional result shape. No native baseline comparison for the newly extracted helper. The full recorder module emits successfully and pipeline primary-file checking passes. The expanded adjacent resume suite passes 46 cases. No main app build or live device/AppKit/Instruments validation. Explicit composition failure still follows the existing terminal .failed UI path on pause/finalization, which closes the recorder; recoverable join retry/retention must be implemented next. Export cancellation before a raw output path reaches this callback can still orphan a file; owned export-result transfer remains pending.

evidence: Cached News anchor remains visible while history loads, requests immediate highlighting, and preserves its previous message/album row position when full history arrives. Table anchor preservation runs after nonanimated row updates; short-document and stationary focus resolve the current row on the next main-queue turn. Eighteen focused regression tests and twenty existing chat lab tests pass; signed-in UI behavior remains unverified.

Each history emission receives a sequence ID; repeated combineLatest emissions from UI/peer/reaction updates cannot replay its initial transition or focus/preservation command. Existing cached rows take the incremental diff path even when appearance changes require main-queue preparation. Twenty-five focused tests pass; six new regressions fail against the previous fix.

Recording send preparation: a selected trim must be acknowledged before stopping, reading media, closing the recorder or clearing chat recording state. Rejected/empty trim results retain the paused source and selection, publish failure, reload the preview, restore controls and show the existing error alert for retry. Duplicate sends and keyboard-send/resume overlap are guarded; the pending operation is owned/cancelled and weakly references the chat destination to avoid a recorder/interaction retain cycle. Successful acknowledgement clears the applied selection even if the destination has disappeared. Direct audio data refuses false/empty trim results and consumes one result; direct video trim rejects nil/unchanged output and uses finite actual output duration rather than substituting the original file. Empty media returns before scheduling/enqueue. Forty-one exact-source isolated tests pass using real SwiftSignalKit and modeled recorder, exporter, asset-duration, hook and view endpoints. All 41 run against saved pre-change source: 36 fail with 60 assertions. The baseline video helper changes only the return-type annotation to optional for comparison; original fallback behavior is preserved. Adjacent 44 recording-resume tests pass. Full native ChatRecordingState and ChatInputRecordingView primary-file checks pass, and the actual MediaRecorderUI module emits into temporary storage. The ChatController empty-selection branch is tested in isolation; a full ChatController build was not performed. No main app build, live recording/server submission, device UI or Instruments validation. Backend composition/export ownership, finalization failure after an accepted trim and end-to-end send acknowledgement still require follow-up.
Reading is tracked only while the application and window are active and visible; foreground transitions retry tracking.
Delete outcome is preserved from the server; rejected deletion retains the passkey and displays an error.

Creation serializes requests through native authorization and server save; reports nil options/results, malformed options and system failures; user cancellation is quiet; closing disposes requests and ignores stale native callbacks; limit uses >= and IDs remain unique. Eleven actual-controller/delegate tests pass; all eleven fail on baseline. Delegate also typechecked against installed AuthenticationServices SDK.

Blocks overlapping sends/verifications, restores loading state after error/progress cancellation, cancels on back/close, ignores stale callbacks, safely handles missing input data and fixes duplicate code-row ordering indices. Eight actual-controller tests pass; all eight fail on baseline.
Session revocation and TTL failures are surfaced; optimistic TTL state reloads on failure.
Uses live session state for switches; serializes updates and reloads optimistic state on error/cancellation; failed revocation keeps the modal open.
Single/all revocation preserves server confirmation; rejection retains sessions and shows an error. Navigation waits for loaded empty state and only pops this controller if it is current.
Premium users and bot exceptions are decoded by exact category ID instead of enabling both for any category. Actual update-closure regression tests included.

Picker result is final selection: deselected peers/categories are removed and existing categories are not duplicated. Retains selected existing peer metadata and loads new group member counts. Eight privacy tests pass; seven fail on baseline.
Guard original media-view child indices for both transition directions; missing children use the existing fallback animation.
Compose local-status and path lookup as one cancellable save signal, avoiding synchronous outer subscription replacement cancelling the path wait.
Ignore stale close animation completions using presentation generation and active viewer identity; old/repeated immediate closes cannot clear a newer viewer or resume PiP twice.
32 isolated tests pass, 15 fail on pre-fix snapshots. GalleryUI typechecked against existing DerivedData; no main app build, file-dialog integration or signed-in visual tests.
Reselecting the visible tab cancels a pending tab-ready subscription so its later completion cannot switch away from the requested tab.
Five isolated tests pass, one fails on pre-fix snapshot. PeerInfoUI typechecked against existing DerivedData. This is a narrow tab-selection audit, not complete profile-screen coverage.
Search now forwards the active media tags and reply-thread ID instead of always searching photos/videos across all topics.
Six isolated tests pass; three fail on pre-fix snapshot. PeerMediaUI typechecked against existing DerivedData. No signed-in topic search validation.

Shared pagination helper retains the engine continuation state and cumulative messages, rejects overlapping/exhausted page requests, cancels with the query subscription and handles synchronous/reentrant callbacks. Actual bottom-scroll routing is covered; no live table visual validation.
Search retains continuation state and loads further pages from bottom scroll. An open but empty search field no longer prevents ordinary history paging.
Grid/list search harness: sixteen tests pass, nine fail on original pre-audit sources; six fail on the preceding scope fix. PeerMediaUI typechecks against existing build dependencies.

Assigns session-local synthetic message IDs by full MediaId using a lock-protected mapping, so truncation, signed IDs and concurrent callbacks cannot collide. Marks synthetic messages Local, includes message namespace in row IDs, and removes repeated bot results while preserving result order.

Playback uses full resource identity and a full media-ID player key, avoiding false matches when a picker is recreated and its synthetic IDs restart. Eighteen focused tests pass; twelve fail on pre-fix snapshots. No real audio playback validation.

Saved-music loading state now follows the core data state; loading alongside existing shared results no longer inserts a duplicate section. Cached/reloading rows remain visible while the request is pending.

Bottom scrolling requests additional saved-music, shared-audio and bot-search pages. Shared queries retain continuation state; bot pages retain offsets, deduplicate results, stop on empty/repeated offsets and cancel on query replacement or modal disposal. Fourteen new pagination tests and eighteen existing identity tests pass; PeerMediaUI typechecks. Native scrolling and live playback remain unverified.
Audio-picker rows match the playing resource; ordinary shared-media rows retain message-based matching.

Modal rows use the supplied Send context menu instead of falling through to ordinary message actions. Validated through extracted production conditions and PeerMediaUI typechecking; no native menu visual test.

ProfileSavedMusicContext leaves loading on request failure or empty completion and allows retry; reload retains visible rows. First-page retries request offset zero even with cached files, and late cached data is published after failure. Empty successful pages stop paging. Child disposable installation preserves reentrant request ownership.

Thirteen isolated loading/cache/picker-state tests pass, eleven fail against original snapshots; two also fail against the initial loading fix. Other saved-music mutations and live server behavior remain pending.

Final TelegramCore source typechecks against existing build dependencies. An earlier attempt was invalidated by editing this file during compilation; the fresh completed check reports exit 0. Main app not built.

ProfileSavedMusicContext keeps nextOffset from raw server document count instead of visible parsed/deduplicated files. Pages merge by full MediaId, preserve ordering and refresh duplicate metadata; unsupported or overlapping documents still advance the cursor. Empty raw pages stop pagination, failed pages retry the same cursor, and an unexpected not-modified response with hash zero preserves visible data and remains retryable.

Request generation plus a child disposable installed before loading-state publication prevents observer-triggered reload from being overwritten by an outer request. Cache/network callbacks require their generation; state guards after cache/loading publication abandon superseded work.

Cache reads are limited to first-page requests, cancelled when superseded or when a server result arrives, and owned separately from writes. Loading the next page preserves a pending first-page cache write. Both cache lifetimes and the network request are disposed on context deinit.

Twenty-four saved-music/picker checks pass, including eleven additions. Seven cases fail against the pre-pagination snapshot (thirteen assertions). SavedMusic.swift passes a native primary-file typecheck with the other TelegramCore sources as declaration context (exit 0). A broader all-file core typecheck was explicitly terminated after focused validation passed (exit 143), so it is not a completed module check. Live network/UI, optimistic mutation reconciliation and whole-app leak validation remain pending.

Add/remove helpers now change cached lists, saved-ID preferences and profile header music only after a true server response. Rejected additions propagate error; removals preserve their existing NoError API. Preferences update independently of page-cache existence, moving the first song updates the header, and removing it promotes the next cached song.

Profile mutations invalidate outstanding page/cache work and block pagination until all subscribed mutations settle. The last completion, error or disposal refreshes from offset zero. Optimistic state changes start on subscription; apply:false retains its explicit immediate local-only behavior. Nested state callbacks preserve request-start order; cancelled queued operations are not sent. This does not serialize server completion or guarantee a cancelled RPC cannot execute remotely.

Saving/removing through another peer profile context changes the account library without optimistically mutating that other profile. Self-anchor moves are no-ops; context and cache share deduplication and missing-anchor placement. Repeated visible removals do not decrement the count again. Partial-list membership and placement remain provisional until authoritative refresh.

Forty-seven harness cases pass, including twenty-three mutation additions. Twenty-one cases fail against the pre-mutation snapshot, with fifty-one assertion failures and no crashes. SavedMusic.swift passes its final native primary-file typecheck (exit 0). Actual context and mutation bodies use real SwiftSignalKit; network, Postbox and file-reference revalidation are simulated. No main app build, signed-in UI check or whole-app leak measurement.

System and in-app seeks now share validated timestamp handling: finite inputs and positive finite duration, clamped positions/progress, position divided by duration, updated elapsed-time status, and stopped pre-seek interpolation. Playing/paused/buffering metadata remains intact; invalid inputs produce no player command or notification.
Weak listener removal uses identity and prunes already-cleared weak entries, including deinitialization, while preserving other live listeners.

Twelve seek tests and eleven combined inline-player lifecycle tests pass; eleven and eight respectively fail against original snapshots. AudioPlayerCore typechecks against existing dependencies. Native playback and system media controls were not exercised.

Stopping clears buffering and disposes the resource-range source. Source events are delivered on main before entering the shared Promise, so replacing/clearing a resource terminates queued old emissions before they can enter UI subscriptions. Both queued stop and next-resource cases fail without this ordering fix and pass with it.
Nineteen combined buffering/list lifecycle tests pass; AudioPlayerCore and AudioPlayerUI typecheck. Decoder status/timebase/end callbacks and real playback remain pending.

Playback generation plus player identity guards suppress obsolete status/timebase/resource/end callbacks. Child disposables are installed before subscribing so synchronous callbacks that replace playback cannot overwrite the new subscriptions; startup rechecks ownership after externally observable state/buffer/timebase/status work.

Stop invalidates session identity before pausing the old decoder, clears status/timebase/resource-observation subscriptions and neighbor prefetches, clears the clock, and stops interpolation before publishing stopped state. Reentry cannot stop a replacement timer. The separate APSongItem fetch request remains a pending ownership review.

Interpolation uses the decoder status generation timestamp and rate, matching iOS scrubber timing, rather than adding a fixed amount per timer tick. Finite positive duration/rate validation, timestamp clamping, explicit timer replacement invalidation and captured session/item identity prevent stale or out-of-bounds updates.

Eighteen session harness tests pass and seventeen fail on the pre-fix snapshot; nineteen buffering and twelve seek regression tests also pass. AudioPlayerCore typechecks. The harness controls timer firing and decoder signals; full playlist reentrancy, real playback and Instruments remain pending.

APSongItem.pullResource is now cold and each subscription owns both its fetch request and resource observers. Disposal, stop, early consumer completion and source completion release that caller's fetch even when the playlist retains the song. Removed the item-wide fetchDisposable and eager fetch() side effect.

The signal captures MediaBox/resource/reference/location/extension values rather than the item, avoiding accidental song retention while allowing a returned signal to remain usable. Existing complete/fetching/paused/remote mappings are preserved.

Thirteen resource ownership tests pass; eleven fail on the pre-fix snapshot. The integrated case executes actual controller stop and preserves a separately subscribed explicit download. AudioPlayerCore typechecks. MediaBox source confirms disposal releases the individual full-range fetch/context; real network and UI integration remain unverified.

Playlist request generation is distinct from decoder lifetime. Song binding, dequeue and delegate notifications reject superseded requests while normal stop/cleanup during completion still allows remaining completion listeners. Child song-state subscription installation preserves the newest binding during synchronous emissions.

Completion coalesces recursive calls, stops before final Now Playing clearing, and abandons old cleanup if a callback starts a newer request. Finish stops only its own request before advancing. Initial negative selection is normalized to the first actual playlist index.
Repeat-all restarts a single-track queue; repeat-none ends at the correct boundary in normal and reversed order. Compared with iOS PeerMessagesMediaPlaylist, which wraps only for .all looping.

Nineteen playlist tests pass, thirteen fail against the pre-fix snapshot. Eighteen prior playback-session tests also pass. AudioPlayerCore typechecks. Shuffle, playlist merge mutations, subclass overrides, native UI and system command ownership remain pending.

ControlCenter uses a weak active owner plus a stable owner token, so old updates/cleanup/deinit cannot reclaim or erase newer Now Playing state. Player start/resume explicitly activates ownership; inactive initialization does not register handlers. Cleanup clears only its own active system presentation.

Command targets are registered idempotently and removed by non-nil owned tokens. Registration generations reject retained callbacks after removal/reactivation; weak captures at both command and APController bridge layers avoid unowned-reference crashes. Next and Previous availability use their respective inputs.

Commands execute on the main queue, validate seek event type/finite position, and report callback success/failure. Background deinit snapshots targets/owner identity and queues cleanup without retaining the deinitializing object; token checks prevent queued cleanup from clearing a newer owner.

Twenty system-control cases pass, sixteen fail against the prior class including two unowned-reference process crashes. Two additional start/resume activation tests pass and fail previously; twenty playback-session and nineteen playlist cases pass. AudioPlayerCore typechecks against native SDK interfaces. Actual OS controls and artwork behavior remain pending.

APItem stores decoder status before publishing observable state, so synchronous observers see the matching timestamp/rate and a nested newer status is not overwritten when the outer setter returns. Now Playing uses interpolated state timing, bounds finite duration/elapsed/rate, publishes zero rate for nonplaying states and marks stopped playback explicitly.

ControlCenter observes only the current cover resource and loads a complete native image once per resource/session. It reuses cached artwork across progress ticks; pending completion merges into the latest metadata rather than captured song timing. Takeover, resource replacement, clear and deinit dispose observation; owner/resource generation guards reject obsolete queued completions. The subscription retains resource identity, not the song.

Artwork no longer copies the image to a temporary JPEG on every progress update. MediaBox.resourceData observes availability without starting a new fetch. AppKit image creation/publication runs on main. A corrupt complete image is not repeatedly reopened on progress ticks; playback reactivation can retry it. macOS 10.13.2 artwork-key guards preserve the module deployment target.

Forty-one system-control/metadata/artwork cases and twelve seek cases pass. Eight metadata additions fail against the pre-metadata snapshot; ten of thirteen artwork additions fail against the pre-cache snapshot. Final AudioPlayerCore native typecheck reports exit 0. Harness uses real SwiftSignalKit and native NSImage loading with simulated MediaBox and OS metadata/commands. No native Control Center rendering, main-app build or whole-app leak validation.

APChatVoiceController.play records the expected decoder generation before calling super and marks content consumed only if that exact request and song still own playback. Stops, observer-driven replacement and same-object restarts cannot let the outer abandoned call mark a stale message.

Voice consumption installs a child MetaDisposable before starting the signal and rechecks playback after disposing the previous child. Synchronous signal start or disposal reentry preserves a newer request instead of overwriting/cancelling it. The playback generation is fileprivate for this same-file subclass; public API is unchanged.

Twenty-eight playback-session cases pass including eight voice-consumption cases; seven voice cases fail on the preceding source (ten assertions). Tests execute actual override and base playback methods with real SwiftSignalKit and simulated receipt/decoder APIs. Active controller deinit releases its pending mark. AudioPlayerCore native typecheck reports exit 0. Real listened/expiry behavior and whole-app leak assessment remain pending.

Playlist merge remaps shuffle history through stable item IDs and drops deleted/out-of-bounds history entries. Current selection is preserved by identity, with fallback recovery from the active song if the stored index is stale. Deletion selects the nearest surviving prior-queue neighbor in playback order, handles a sole survivor, and wraps at the boundary only for repeat-all; a paused/waiting/stopped deleted item completes without starting another track.

The chat-history callback no longer separately calls finish after merge already handled a deleted current item. This prevents duplicate completion/clearing and repeat-one restarting an unrelated item. Merge relies on the existing generation-aware dequeue/complete paths, so stop and completion callbacks can safely select newer playback.

Retained selection changes notify state listeners when index/count or updated entries change, refreshing both player-view and system transport availability even while paused. Existing notification generation checks preserve a selection made by a listener. Empty transitions do not republish player state.

Thirty-six playlist cases pass, including seventeen transition additions; twelve additions fail against the pre-merge snapshot. Twenty-eight playback-session/voice cases also pass. Final AudioPlayerCore typecheck reports exit 0. iOS uses message-ID playback history and wraps ordered automatic navigation only with all looping; custom shuffle semantics differ and remain under review. Native UI, updated-resource replacement and shuffle-cycle policy are not validated by this pass.

APEntry song equality now uses the existing isEqualMessages comparator instead of message ID alone, allowing stable-version, media and author changes to produce updated playlist entries. Source inspection verified proccessEntries uses entry equality to produce update indices.

Merge retains the active APSongItem for unchanged resource IDs while adopting updated entry, title, performer, resource reference and extension. The decoder/status/state subscription stays attached to that same object, so currentSong and player state no longer diverge after a list update. Metadata storage remains externally read-only; mutation is confined to the model/file.

A changed resource replaces active playback through the existing generation-safe dequeue path. If playback is paused or otherwise inactive, the old session completes without playing the replacement; an explicit subsequent dequeue uses the new resource. New selections from stop observers remain authoritative. Same-position reinsertions publish updated metadata even when count/index do not change.

Forty-six playlist and twenty-eight playback-session/voice checks pass. Ten new edit cases use actual metadata adoption, merge/history callbacks, APEntry equality and production isEqualMessages with modeled Message/media/peer data; nine fail on the prior snapshot (twenty-three assertions). Final AudioPlayerCore native typecheck reports exit 0. iOS SharedMediaPlayer rebuilds playback for changed playback data; this implementation preserves the decoder across metadata-only changes keyed by resource ID. Native decoder/Postbox edits, artwork/PiP integration and whole-app leak validation remain pending.

Tracks the subscribed controller independently of NavigationHeader.contextObject, which is overwritten before view update. Reuse detaches the previous listener; delegate/render/buffering callbacks require the currently observed and displayed controller.

Shutdown cancels buffering, detaches the listener and invalidates observed identity before stopping; repeated/stale completion cannot close a newer player. Deinit detaches the listener and disposes subscriptions.

Eleven production-method lifecycle harness tests pass; eight fail against original UI/core snapshots. AudioPlayerUI typechecks. Object-release tests use simulated UI/header/player dependencies and are not a whole-app leak assessment.

Progress rejects non-finite values and clamps finite values to 0...1 for playback and fetching. Waiting clears old progress; stopped playback restores playback styling. Shared twelve-case control harness passes; native rendering remains pending.

Clears buffering before observing a replacement controller and on nil status. Uses bounded offset-preserving ranges through the existing range-aware progress control; empty/unknown/full buffers clear overlays. Rejects old-song delegates even from the current controller.

Expanded inline lifecycle harness passes fourteen tests; all three additions fail against preceding implementation. Shared buffering harness covers actual updateStatus in both player views; native rendering remains pending.

Detaches the previous audio listener, migrates navigation/table/window ownership and synchronizes the active song. Stale controller and previous-message callbacks cannot replace the active PiP; completed/stopped media cannot reappear on later scrolling.

Reuses the media subscription, preview and mouse handlers while the same message and resource remain visible. Avoids redundant timebase resets. Hiding cancels resource updates; matching hide completion clears media/preview and removes the view. Presentation generation prevents old hide completions from removing a reopened PiP.

Mouse actions target the bound player, including cleanup after completion that may start another global player. Deinit releases subscriptions, listeners, handlers and the view; the stored navigation weak reference avoids constructing a weak reference during deallocation.

Eighteen production-controller harness tests pass, fifteen fail against the original source. Final isolated PiP source typechecks against built dependencies plus its actual internal ChatControllerKind declaration. Whole ChatUI typecheck remains incomplete: fresh temporary analytics/recorder interfaces resolved initial errors, but cached InputDataUI and other interfaces still mismatch concurrent source changes. Live server normalization, reverse response/commit/replay ordering and accepted-but-unobserved cancellation remain unverified; dependency tags alone do not establish local ordering.

Localization layout, calendar accessibility, global preference changes mid-picker, extreme dates, actual date-preview fetching and suggested-birthday modal lifecycle remain partial.

Profile photo/video updates now share one owned operation from image preparation or video generation through editor results and upload. MediaObjectToAvatar no longer self-retains until a successful result. start() now returns a cold signal; each subscription creates and retains its own generator until completion/disposal, without retaining the originating generator object. Cancelled/failed/empty operations and unused signals no longer depend on a later successful value to break a self-cycle. Ten exact-wrapper tests use real SwiftSignalKit with controlled generation and weak lifetime probes; all pass. The original wrapper is tested with expensive rendering/fetch setup replaced by the same controlled endpoint, retaining its actual holder/afterNext ownership logic; it fails eight cases with ten assertions, including unsubscribed work, cancellation, empty/failure lifetime and shared-operation behavior. The normal successful baseline cleanup is allowed its original main-queue delay. Full MediaObjectToAvatar native primary-file checking passes. Underlying AVAssetWriter/decoder/fetch cancellation, queued conversion work and temporary-file cleanup are not proven by this wrapper harness.

StickerToMp4Context now consumes preparation once, reports exporter/renderer/metadata/first-frame/thumbnail/pixel-buffer/render/finalization failure, and cancels fetch/export work with a shared atomic cancellation flag that is visible while the conversion queue is busy. Wrapper cancellation/deinit invalidates the flag before queue cleanup. Output completion is fenced; failed thumbnails and rejected output paths are deleted, while successful outputs transfer to the consumer and survive context release. The first rendered frame is reused, later frames receive the prior frame for decoder/cache dependencies, and a short WebM finishes at its detected endpoint instead of treating decoder end as a render error. Twenty-three tests compile the complete production StickerToMp4Context and actual frame sequence with real SwiftSignalKit, CoreMedia and filesystem operations; rendering, resource fetching and writer completion are controlled fixtures. All pass. Full MediaObjectToAvatar native primary-file checking passes. No executable original-context comparison was made because its nested writer/monolithic synchronous loop has a different interface; baseline failing count is zero/unknown. Real Lottie/WebM/WebP decoder behavior, failed download signaling, empty-background signals, extremely long exports, image allocation failures and live UI remain unverified.

Avatar source preparation now uses a typed fetchedMediaResource path instead of swallowing fetch errors. Fetch completion without next is valid; resource data is read after accepted completion, incomplete data is ignored, one complete path is consumed, and empty data completion becomes failure. The helper retains MediaBox rather than AccountContext. Static sticker decoding/read failures and empty backgrounds produce a terminal result; repeated starts/data/background updates do not repeat work. GIF/video sources validate a copied video, extract a transformed JPEG thumbnail and only then publish both paths; copy/decode/thumbnail failure never publishes a fake path. Prepared files are owned until takeFiles transfers them and are removed if unclaimed. makeAvatarVideo now routes static stickers through photo handling, and static failure/unexpected results complete instead of returning a never-ending inner signal. The profile controller uses this shared adapter. Thirty-six tests pass: 22 exact-source typed-fetch/source lifecycle cases, 8 full-adapter cases and 6 native AVFoundation/ImageIO/filesystem cases. Native cases verify real copied MP4 bytes/duration, JPEG readability/dimensions, missing/invalid/directory sources, unclaimed cleanup and transferred-file survival. The original adapter fails 4 of its 8 cases with 7 assertions; the other 28 preparation tests have no original-source executable comparison. Native checks pass for MediaObjectToAvatar, AvatarMediaPreparation, MakeAvatarVideo and the profile caller. Live network/database ordering, real WebP decoding, native UI error feedback and file cleanup after paths have already transferred remain unverified. Generator terminal-result follow-up: MediaObjectToAvatar.start now forwards progress until one successful result or explicit failure, then completes/disposes once. A source that completes without a result emits an explicit failure. Animated source failures retain the failed status, and static adapters do not translate terminal failure into never(). Four additional wrapper tests bring the suite to 14 passing cases. The immediate pre-change wrapper fails the four new cases with 9 assertions. The original pre-ownership wrapper fails 12 of all 14 cases with 19 assertions; the normal successful original cleanup retains its main-queue timing allowance. Rendering remains controlled in this lifetime suite. Typed source-error follow-up: StickerToMp4Context now consumes avatarMediaResourcePath, so failed downloads terminate conversion; an empty background also produces failure when preparation completes without a tuple. The completed callback distinguishes preparation that has actually started rendering so it cannot reject an ongoing export. Three additional full-context cases bring that suite to 26 passing cases; fetch endpoint behavior is modeled there and separately exercised with real SwiftSignalKit in avatar-media-preparation. Native full-source checking passes.

Avatar bitmap generation now uses a local failable Core Graphics context. Color gradients and emoji bitmap creation no longer force-unwrap failed output. Pattern backgrounds wait for completed decodable data, accept one final image, dispose the source and reject missing data/context/image instead of accepting a loading placeholder. Thirty-five rendering tests pass: 12 native Core Graphics/Core Video pixel/geometry cases, 12 controlled allocation/locking/extraction cases, and 11 exact-helper pattern cases using real SwiftSignalKit/ImageIO with a modeled transform. Native primary-file checks pass for MediaObjectToAvatar and AvatarImageRendering. Full app rendering, display/codec diversity, actual memory pressure and shared DrawingContext internals remain unverified; the shared pattern renderer still has its own unchecked allocation path.

Empty-background follow-up: combineLatest waits for both sources to complete, so a completed background without an image previously kept a pending sticker download alive. Two synchronous/asynchronous pending-download cases per path fail on the immediately preceding snapshot (4 cases, 8 assertions) and pass after the fix. All 29 conversion cases and all 39 media-preparation cases pass. Full native MediaObjectToAvatar primary-file checking passes. This covers an explicitly completed empty background, not a wallpaper source that never emits or completes.

Full native primary-file checking passes against cached dependencies. Apple documentation and telegram-ios MediaEditorVideoAVAssetWriter corroborate readiness-driven supply. Live codec/device diversity and every supported sticker format remain unverified.

VideoAvatarModalController now delegates trimmed video export to an owned asynchronous exporter. Trim bounds/durations/non-finite values are validated; thumbnail time is clamped inside the selected range and the uploaded key-frame timestamp is relative to the trim start, then bounded by actual output duration.
