Session creation and MP4 support, thumbnail decoding/destination/finalization, final export status/error and readable output duration/video tracks are checked. Failed/cancelled/unclaimed partial files are removed, including files recreated by late completion after cancellation; successful paths transfer to the existing consumer contract. Timers stop on termination and hold the operation weakly; progress is finite and clamped. Startup uses Queue.justDispatch because Queue.async executes inline on its own queue and could start work before a cancellation handle was installed. Thirty-three isolated tests pass: 21 full-exporter controlled AVFoundation/ImageIO cases using real SwiftSignalKit/timers/filesystem, 8 native CMTime range cases and 4 real AVFoundation cases. A generated H.264 source produced a readable 0.6-second trimmed MP4 with a 0.3-second relative cover timestamp and a readable 640x640 JPEG; invalid preset, empty composition and cancellation after thumbnail creation were also checked natively. Six safe timing cases run against exact earlier timing expressions from commit 6bb9f7ec39259d7a4537820620f775bd82b8becf; five fail with nine assertions. This comparison does not execute the full old export lifecycle or reproduce its forced-unwrap crashes. Native primary-file checks pass for EditedAvatarVideoExport and the complete VideoAvatarModalController; the harness fully compiles the exporter. No app build or live editor UI validation.

Video avatar preparation now returns the copied composition track, preserving its preferred transform, and both preview/export instructions reference that track rather than the source asset track. Missing/invalid input returns an explicit terminal error instead of leaving the caller without a signal. Geometry uses the transformed source rectangle and normalizes its origin, preserving reflections and arbitrary affine transforms instead of guessing one of four rotations. Crop mapping validates finite nonzero video/view/selection geometry, bounds the crop, keeps positive encoder dimensions for tiny selections and scales the selected region to the rounded output dimensions. The controller rejects unavailable crop composition before export and thumbnail generation; invalid Enter remains consumed by the modal. Thumbnail count conversion is checked. Twenty-six tests pass: 14 native Core Graphics geometry cases, 5 native preparation/export cases, 3 real mirrored/rotated pixel comparisons and 4 exact selectVideoAvatar routing cases with modeled modal/window endpoints. A source composition using track ID 42 is copied into a new track and renders successfully with instructions targeting the new ID. A mirrored 320x320 crop exports a readable MP4 whose pixels match its preview. Seven native crop/routing cases run against the exact earlier methods from commit 6bb9f7ec39259d7a4537820620f775bd82b8becf; five fail with nine assertions. Native full-controller and helper primary-file checks pass. The crop comparison retains the current preparation fixture and substitutes only the old crop method; routing compares the actual old selection function. No full UI/AppKit presentation, every crop interaction, real-world portrait/VFR/codec matrix or Instruments coverage is claimed.

Avatar playback now seeks to the actual trim start rather than adding an offset proportional to the entire source duration, sets forwardPlaybackEndTime, and clamps suspended seeks inside the selected interval. Each playback generation owns its periodic/end callbacks; obsolete or hidden-editor callbacks cannot move the playhead or restart playback. Reappearance preserves pause state. Initial min/max trim distances are normalized for short clips and do not depend on laid-out width; invalid/sub-millisecond durations reject initialization. Moving a trim interval preserves its duration at both boundaries. Thirty-three exact-source isolated tests pass with real CoreMedia/SwiftSignalKit and modeled player, notification and control endpoints. The original safe comparison contains 32 applicable cases (the new sub-millisecond helper case is excluded); 23 fail with 35 assertions. Native helper, scrubber and full-controller primary-file checks pass. Native AVPlayer seek/event scheduling, live editor gestures and Instruments remain unverified.

Layout, all drag paths, clicks/long presses, darkened trim masks, thumbnails and cover preview/dot positions share that coordinate mapping. Playhead centers clamp to the selected range; zero/tiny bounds cannot create negative sizes. Detached controls, zero-width tracks and non-finite pointer coordinates do not mutate selection. Frame drags clamp at trim endpoints and can move back immediately. Twenty-eight exact-source isolated tests pass: 24 layout/gesture cases using modeled view/window endpoints, two native Core Graphics mask-pixel cases, and two actual controller preview-position expressions. All 28 run against the pre-geometry snapshot; 26 fail with 71 assertions. The adjacent 33 playback cases still pass, and native full scrubber/controller primary-file checks pass. No full app build or live AppKit hit-testing/animation validation. Extremely narrow but positive hit regions still need a usability/zoom review; asynchronous cover-preview lifecycle is a separate remaining audit.
